Method of Attack: Distributed via massive spam campaign with emails containing JavaScript downloader masquerading as JPG files
JavaScript file executes PowerShell and Bitsadmin commands to download and run ransomware executable
Ransomware encrypts files appending .avdn extension and drops ransom note with TOR payment site link
Ransomware-as-a-Service (RaaS) model recruiting affiliates to distribute ransomware via spam, network compromise, and exploit kits
Attack Vector: Spam email with malicious JavaScript attachment disguised as JPG file
Indicators of Compromise: Spam email subjects: 'Your new photo?', 'Do you like my photo?'
